newsitem.title: PAPUA NEW GUINEA: Two die in Papua New Guinea election violence.
newsitem.headline: Two die in Papua New Guinea election violence.

text.p: Two people have been killed and several others injured in violence during early polling in Papua New Guinea's two-week long national elections, officials said on Wednesday.

Police said one man died when he was hit by a vehicle fleeing a stone-throwing mob at Mount Hagen in Western Highlands province. The driver of the vehicle had earlier tried to take ballot papers from a polling booth.

On Bougainville island, 800 km (500 miles) northeast of the capital Port Moresby, a man was shot dead and two others were wounded when they were ambushed by separatist rebels trying to disrupt polling on the island, police said.
The vote is seen as crucial to the future stability of the South Pacific nation, which experenced the worst crisis in its 21-year independent history after an army mutiny in April.

Faced with the revolt and violent civil protests, Prime Minister Sir Julius Chan was forced to step aside over plans to use British-led mercenaries to quash a nine-year secessionist uprising on Bougainville.
Chan resumed power two weeks ago in time for the elections, which began on Saturday.

Up to three million citizens can vote and voting across the country will take up to two weeks to allow voters from remote areas to reach polling stations. A new government is not expected to be formed until late July.
In other violent incidents, police arrested five men who hijacked a helicopter on Tuesday and forced the foreign pilot to fly to polling areas in Western Highlands province.
They said the men, who held up the pilot at gunpoint and ripped out the helicopter's communications, had tried to disrupt voting at a number of polling booths.
In Chimbu, also in the Highlands, another man was cut badly with bush knives and axes when he and others tried to steal ballot papers.
Polling officials said voting in a number of regions had been delayed due to the late arrival of ballot papers.

In Port Moresby, where voting only took a day, popular lord mayor and sitting parliamentary member Bill Skate took an early lead when counting of votes began on Tuesday, according to a preliminary tally.
Skate, who is leader of the emerging People's National Congress, has indicated he wants to challenge Chan for the prime ministership of the country.
